title: How Showmob works
summary: What this site is, the short path from idea to shared link, and what the same small content language also unlocks.

blocks.title: One link for an idea worth showing
blocks.body: Showmob turns a structured page into a normal website URL. You write the idea as JSON (or in Studio), the app renders it, and anyone with the link can read it. No slide deck. No separate presentation app.

blocks.heading: What this is (and what it is not)
blocks.body:
This is a small Vite + React app. Live site: showmob.vercel.app. Source: github.com/wyrmspire/showmob.

It exists so Chris can share an idea as a readable page instead of rebuilding a deck every time. Pages are content files. The renderer is shared. Themes are token sets, not one-off CSS.

It is intentionally thin. It is not Mira, not Edgerite, and not a full CMS. Collaboration, search, analytics, and multi-tenant accounts are out of scope for now. A later thin data layer may store artifacts and publish status without growing into those products.

nodes.title: Write
nodes.detail: A schemaVersion 1 JSON file under app/src/content, or a Studio export that matches the same contract.

nodes.title: Render
nodes.detail: Each block has a type. Trusted widgets draw it. Browse is the whole page; a slideshow is only a block when you need paced slides.

nodes.title: Publish
nodes.detail: Set status to published, commit, merge to main. Vercel deploys. Production lists published pages only; draft and preview files stay in the repo.

blocks.heading: Three ways to use it
blocks.caption: Same site. Different jobs.

Open any published page and scroll
A normal document with the author’s theme.
Present
Find a slideshow block and step through it
Paced slides inside the same page — not a global Present mode.
Author
Open Studio (local / author tools)
Arrange blocks, validate, export JSON. Drafts stay in this browser until you export.

slides.title: Content is the page
slides.body: Most new pages are JSON artifacts, not custom React. Add a valid file and the build picks it up.

slides.title: Browse is the default
slides.body: Shared links open as readable scrolling pages. Theme on the artifact is what visitors see.

slides.title: Publish is a status, not a delete
slides.body: draft → preview → published. Production hides unpublished pages. The files remain in git for authors.

slides.title: Stay thin on purpose
slides.body: Polish the renderer and the content contract first. Add only the data and authoring pieces that prove they earn their complexity.

blocks.heading: What these mechanics also allow
blocks.body: schemaVersion 1 JSON pages, a shared block vocabulary, themes, Browse plus slideshow-as-block, lifecycle status, and series plus hub/tags are a small content language. Beyond one idea → one link, the same pieces compose into courses, explainers, and story worlds—without becoming Mira or Edgerite.

blocks.heading: Jobs the language already fits
blocks.caption: Recipes are named combinations of today’s blocks. A future gallery would make those recipes learnable—it is not shipped yet.
rows: Courses / lessons
Ordered series of pages teaching a subject (already true for the mechanics course).
Works today with series.order.
Explainers & comparisons
Compose blocks into jobs: hero+text+diagram+exercise, or comparison+table+callout.
Recipes are patterns on today’s vocabulary; gallery is later.
Story worlds
Separate stable world pages (characters, places, refs) from telling (ordered prose against them).
World vs telling is the practice; graph tooling is not shipped.
Cross-page exploration
Named slugs and manual links today; series for straight reading, hub/tags to wander.
Real references and “appears in…” backlinks are later growth.
Agent-friendly authoring
Search before create; compose and validate JSON; publish a shareable URL.
Prove the language with real content, not only meta pages about Showmob.
Later thin data
Optional participatory or saved state without becoming a CMS.
Hinted on the roadmap; not a live store yet.

columns.name: World (stable)
columns.detail: Character, place, and reference pages that hold facts. Agents and authors read them before a scene and update them after publish.

columns.name: Telling (prose)
columns.detail: Ordered scenes written against the world. Metaphor and voice live here; facts stay on world pages. Series for straight-through reading; hub and tags to wander.

items.title: Portable pages + honest production catalog
items.detail: JSON artifacts, Browse + slideshow blocks, five themes, series and hub/tags, published-only public list, author theme on share links.

items.title: Share and navigate better
items.detail: Section deep links, clearer copy-link, and per-page link previews so a shared URL looks like that page.

items.title: Gallery, references, thin data
items.detail: A learnable block gallery and named recipes; typed page references with backlinks so broken links fail validation and pages can show “appears in…”; optional store for artifacts and light participatory state. Keep the JSON contract; avoid Mira-scale features.

blocks.title: Local vs production
blocks.body: On your machine, npm run dev can show draft and preview pages and theme audition. Production (and a normal production build) shows published pages only. Studio drafts and exercise answers stay in the browser until you export or refresh clears them.

blocks.title: Story worlds are one use of the same language
blocks.body: World vs telling above is the practice on today’s blocks. A separate growth sketch goes deeper on arcs, personalities, hubs, and participatory entries—local-only limits today, thin data later. It is not a claim that story worlds ship end-to-end.

items.label: Story worlds as data entries
items.detail: Growth sketch: arcs, personalities, open world, and participatory entries—using the same language, with honest local-only limits today.

blocks.heading: Start with one published page
blocks.body: Pick a page from the hub, try any slideshow on it, then open Studio only when you are ready to shape a new artifact. If something here is still confusing, fix this guide first — it is the shared map.
